numerical_failure.observed_behavior: With NaN values in the input image, unwrap_phase can hang (fail to terminate) because floating point comparisons in the C unwrapping code (unwrap_2d_ljmu.c) are not NaN-safe.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: unwrap_phase should not hang on input containing NaN; NaN values should be treated as an implicit mask. Weird results after NaNs are introduced are acceptable, but it should not freeze. After the fix, the masked-array result should equal the result on an array with NaNs at the same masked positions (test_unwrap_3d_nan uses np.testing.assert_equal).
trigger_conditions: input image to unwrap_phase contains NaN values
NaN entries present in the wrapped phase image (chelsea-derived float example in the discussion uses np.angle(np.exp(1j*image)))
oracle_clues: issue#3831 describes the hang on NaN input; PR#8193 adds an implicit NaN mask (nan_mask, with image_not_masked[nan_mask] = 0) and its release note says NaN values could previously cause the code to hang
tests in tests/skimage/restoration/test_unwrap.py (test_unwrap_3d_nan) were updated to use np.testing.assert_equal (exact equality) in the fixing commit
Maintainer comment: it is okay to have weird results after NaNs are introduced; it just shouldn't freeze

category_specific_evidence: Issue #3831 notes floating point comparisons in the C code (unwrap_2d_ljmu.c) are not NaN safe, and that the algorithm is tripped up by them.
Issue #3831 states that NaN values could cause unwrap_phase to hang, per the PR release note.
PR #8193 'Add implicit NaN mask' masks any NaNs in the input image as an implicit mask, combined with any explicit masked-array mask.
The diff sets image_not_masked[nan_mask] = 0 when NaNs are present, so NaN entries are replaced with 0 before unwrapping.
The new test test_unwrap_3d_nan compares unwrap_phase on a masked array against unwrap_phase on an array with NaNs at the same masked positions, using np.testing.assert_equal (exact equality).
The mask is computed with np.isnan, replacing the previous all-zero default mask, with no memory implication per the discussion.
Benchmark on the chelsea image shows about 34.7 ms on main vs 35.3 ms with the PR, described as negligible performance impact.
reproduction_risks: Passages do not state the dtype or precision of the failing input beyond the chelsea example, which uses float values from rgb2gray/img_as_float without specifying a dtype in the bug text.
Signed zero, +/-inf and subnormal handling are not discussed in the passages.
The hang is reported only qualitatively; no specific input values or expected unwrapped output are given beyond the test's equality check.
